thread:
maria: opening ticket from customer — they report the trace panel shows only the root span for a subset of requests and the request-id -> trace link returns "no trace found". Examples customer provided: X-Request-ID: req-9f2c, req-9f2d. Time window: 2025-11-05T14:23:10Z - 2025-11-05T14:30:00Z. Repro steps below.

maria: repro curl they ran:
``
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -H "X-Request-ID: req-9f2c" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '"{\"prompt\":\"hi\"}"
```

maria: console screenshot attached: https://redwood.s3.amazonaws.com/support/screens/req-9f2c-missing-spans.png

raj: assigning — can you paste ingest logs for those request_ids and the exact timestamps? customer says some traces link but spans are missing which suggests partial ingestion or mapping normalization issue.

ellie: heads-up: we rolled trace-mapper v2.3.0 yesterday that now normalizes request ids (lowercase + strip non-alphanum except dashes). If customer headers contain underscores or mixed case, that could produce a mismatch. Can someone dump trace_mappings rows for those ids?

sam: quick SQL to run on prod-read-replica:
``
SELECT request_id, trace_id, array_agg(span_id) as spans
FROM trace_mappings JOIN spans USING (trace_id)
WHERE request_id IN ('req-9f2c','req-9f2d')
GROUP BY request_id, trace_id;
```

maria: ran a quick check — mapping table shows request_id stored as `req_9f2c` (underscore) while incoming header uses `req-9f2c` (dash). Normalization mismatch confirmed.

ellie: that matches my suspicion. v2.3.0 inadvertently rewrites underscores to dashes during normalization, so old mappings (underscore) and new lookups (dash) don't match. Spans are attached to the trace_id, but the request_id -> trace_id lookup misses.

raj: plan: can we hotfix mapper to do a fallback lookup (try raw header, normalized underscore, normalized dash) and backfill alias mappings for the recent window? Need impact estimate.

sam: deploy-bot shows last deploy for trace-mapper:
deploy-bot: trace-mapper v2.3.0 deployed to prod by ellie at 2025-11-04T22:12:10Z — rolling 3/3 completed.

ellie: I can cut v2.3.1 to add fallback lookup and make normalization idempotent. Propose canary 5% immediately, then 25% if metrics look good. I'll also prepare a backfill job to insert alias rows for underscore<->dash for the last 48h. DB write batch estimated ~2m per batch, can run without global lock.

raj: also add mitigation for CS: we can provide a query to search traces by host + time window if customer gives timestamps. That avoids them having to resend requests.

maria: I'll message CS with a short note: apology, explain temporary normalization bug in trace-mapper, ask them to provide the list of affected request-ids and confirm timeframe. Workaround: send an additional header `X-Redwood-Req-Id` with the alternate form or we can run a backfill on their behalf.

ellie: starting PR now. Will post PR link and canary logs here. Backfill job will create alias mappings for the last 48h and update a migration flag to prevent double-inserts.

sam: ops checklist before canary:
- run backfill dry-run to estimate writes and conflicts
- push v2.3.1 to canary 5%
- monitor metric `trace_mapping_miss_count` and `trace_panel_missing_spans` by customer_id
- prepare rollback (v2.3.0) and DB cleanup script
- notify CS when canary is green

maria: CS notified the customer and requested the 20 example request-ids they already provided. I'll update them once canary/backfill are complete.

raj: thanks, team. tagging @oncall for paging if rollback required :thumbsup:

ellie: on it — will post PR + canary logs shortly and follow up here with timestamps for backfill runs.
